review_notes: I read the whole file. I grepped Mathlib for other sigma-compactness or exhaustion concepts and found none that compete with the file's own definitions. IsSigmaCompact, SigmaCompactSpace and CompactExhaustion appear to be the only declarations of their kind. Set.FiniteExhaustion in Mathlib/Data/Set/FiniteExhaustion.lean exhausts a set by finite sets. It is a different concept from CompactExhaustion, which needs compact sets with K n ⊆ interior (K (n+1)) covering a topological space. compactCovering is built from the existing Order `accumulate` rather than from a new notion. The several near-identical countable-union lemmas (iUnion, sUnion, biUnion) are named variants, and the rubric excludes standalone theorem duplication. I found no concrete competing definition that would justify consolidation.
